history.subject: Prove Module.Finite k H^1(X,O_X) for any scheme X with a finite k-morphism \pi : X \to \mathbb{P}^1 (quantified conditional theorem), by running the two-lattice ladder over k[T,T^{-1}] on the Mayer-Vietoris cokernel of the chart-preimage cover: \Gamma(V_0 \cap V_1) is module-finite over the Laurent ring via \pi's app on D_+(X_0X_1), the images Q_0, Q_1 of \Gamma(V_0), \Gamma(V_1) are T- resp. T^{-1}-stable since T = X_1/X_0 restricts from V_0, and V_0 \cap V_1 is the basic open of the pulled-back chart coordinate inside affine V_0, giving surjectivity up to powers. New P1-side inputs (Cohomology/FinitenessP1.lean): the scheme-level basic open of the chart coordinate t = X_j/X_i in Gamma(D_+(X_i)) is the chart overlap; the structure algebra map on D_+(f) is k -> (k[X_0,X_1]_f)_0 -> Gamma(D_+(f)); T, T^{-1} and scalars of the Laurent identification as restrictions from the charts. Derive the instance Module.Finite k H^1(C,O_C) for the challenge curve (consuming exists_isFinite_toP1), keyed on genus's letI spelling — genus is now the dimension of an honestly finite-dimensional space. Axioms: exactly propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound for both the conditional theorem and the curve instance.

Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules, landed as pure algebra (Wave-3 lane L5, the honest algebraic core of Picard separatedness (C1) and rigidified effectivity (C2)): descent data in Sweedler-coring/comodule form (coaction M -> B tensor_A M with counit + coassociativity; dictionary to the classical B tensor B cocycle iso recorded), the descended A-module as the coaction equalizer, and the comparison B tensor_A M_0 -> M an isomorphism — effectivity needs only FLATNESS of A -> B (counit + coassoc make the augmented complex contractible after base change; a strengthening over the textbook statement), faithfulness entering only for Amitsur exactness in degrees <= 1, the unit N = (B tensor N)_0, and uniqueness of descent. Property descent along faithfully flat maps: finite presentation (new to the tree; mathlib only had the algebra form), finite projectivity, and INVERTIBILITY (via dual-commutes-with-base-change for finite projectives, retract argument) — so the descended module of an invertible module is invertible (Module.DescentDatum.invertible_descended, the lane deliverable). Confirmed absent from mathlib v4.31: any Amitsur complex, any effective descent of modules. Unit-cocycle recipe for the Picard consumers documented (toSpanSingleton coaction from a unit of B tensor B; cocycle condition = coassoc).
